name: Tselane Bozović-Quiñonez
role: Barber and part-time hair artist, operates 'The Cut Below' in the Burnished Market
location: The Burnished Market, stall row 14, ground level
description:
Tselane is a tall woman with exceptional posture — the kind that comes from years of standing behind a chair — and hands that move with the constant precise economy of someone who has made roughly forty-thousand cuts in her lifetime and stopped counting. She has her Sotho grandmother's high forehead and her Serbian grandfather's grey-green eyes, and her own hair is an ever-changing showcase for her skills: currently a deep violet with shaved geometric patterns at the temples that she re-cuts every twelve days with mechanical precision. She has color-changing hair geneware — the violet is her default but she can shift it across a spectrum when she's in a creative mood, which she will tell you is a professional statement and not vanity, and she is partially right.

The shop is a two-chair stall wedged between a spice vendor and a counterfeit-data reseller, draped with mirror panels and lit with warm amber strips that make everyone look better than they do outside, which Tselane will tell you is the first thing a barber owes their client. She is direct, opinionated, and runs an informal social-credit system where she remembers every regulars' preferences, history, and most recent life developments. She doesn't offer advice unless asked, but when she offers it, it is specific and often irritatingly accurate.

core_fears: Her hands failing — the tremor she had before the stabilizer implant was the worst year of her life
Becoming irrelevant as automated style-bots get cheaper and better
core_desires: To be recognized as an artist, not just a service provider
To have a real shop, with a door and a sign, not a market stall
coping_mechanisms: The work itself — a clean cut is a form of control
Very dry humor that she deploys to avoid discussing things that actually bother her
blind_spots: Trusts her own reads on people too completely — she's usually right, which makes her worse when she's wrong
Has difficulty asking for help; frames every struggle as a problem she can solve alone
psychology.secret: She was once registered as a freelance data courier — nothing serious, just running encrypted packages across market stalls for extra income. She stopped when a package she carried turned out to contain something that got a person killed two days later. She never knew what it was. She still doesn't know if she was implicated. She has not thought carefully about whether some of her regular clients know.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and confident. Doesn't use more words than needed. Compliments are specific and earned. Criticism is constructive and delivered without apology.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even, unhurried. Lets silences sit — comfortable with them in a way that occasionally unnerves clients.
example_lines: 'You've been growing this out for four months and you came in here looking like that. We're starting over. That's not an insult, that's a diagnosis.'
'I heard that. I'm not going to tell you what to do with it, because you didn't ask. But I heard it.'

story_hooks: A client whispered something in the chair last week that sounded like part of a location code — the client hasn't come back and Tselane has been turning it over in her mind

A well-dressed Tessera mid-manager has been coming in weekly for two months, always cash, always asking specific questions about Burnished Market regulars that are just a little too specific to be casual
narrative_function: Social hub and rumor clearinghouse — the barber chair is where people talk. She is an excellent source of Burnished Market gossip, neighborhood politics, and the general mood of the community. Can be a quest giver for things she's heard in the chair.
augmentations: Color-changing hair geneware (Helix Biosystems, violet default, full spectrum capable). Micro-stabilizer implant in both wrists — suppresses fine tremor for precision work (professional install, saved for two years).
daily_life: Opens the stall at 0900, runs by appointment in the mornings and walk-in in the afternoons, closes when the last client is done which is usually 2000. Thursdays she does hair art — complex structural work that takes hours and which she charges three times her regular rate.
affiliation: Independent; registered vendor in the Burnished Market Traders Collective

decision_rules: What happens in the chair stays in the chair — she will not be a source of gossip about specific clients
Never take a courier job again, for any reason, for any amount
escalation_ladder: State plainly that the conversation is over
Pick up her shears and stop talking entirely

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional warmth, calibrated — she learns them through questions before offering anything of herself
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal and attentive, remembers everything, shows affection through small specific gestures

stress_responses.low: Hair shifts slightly toward red in her color spectrum
stress_responses.medium: Goes very controlled and precise in her movements, conversation dries up
stress_responses.high: Closes the stall early, goes to the market's rooftop smoking terrace, and does not answer messages

contradictions: Says she doesn't get involved in clients' lives, has a drawer full of notes on regulars' situations and whether they're okay
habits: Resharpens her best shears at the end of every day regardless of use
Has a small ELF shrine under the counter — a repurposed power cell with a curl of cut hair inside; she leaves it ambient sound clips of good haircuts going well
breaking_points: Someone touching her tools without permission
Being accused of passing information about a client
